readMe:
THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

CORRECTED AT ITER129, because a later method depends on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
"[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". iter128
called truncation "the worse failure because it looks like success"; the real risk is an agent
SKIMMING PAST an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything. That notice is also the ONLY tokenizer
on this machine (no tiktoken, no anthropic, no transformers), and it is how iter129 calibrated the
size checker: build a file over the cap but under 256 KB, Read it whole, divide bytes by the reported
total. Markdown measured 2.604 B/tok, this file's JSON 2.368.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are six precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive` - and each one asserted its round-trip before this
file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. NO GATE IS TICKED, SO THERE IS STILL NO FEATURE WORK THE LOOP MAY DO — and iter129,
like 127 and 128, spent its increment on the loop's own machinery, found the same way: by obeying step 1
literally and measuring what it actually returned.

  (1) STEP 1 READS THREE FILES AND ITER128'S CHECKER MEASURED ONE. `tools/loop/state.json`, `GATES.md` and
      PLAN.md §14 are all on the step-1 path. iter128 built check-state-size.py for the file it had just
      fixed and stopped there, so two of the three were guarded by nothing — the same unmeasured-assumption
      shape that let the token cap truncate step 1 unnoticed for several iterations, one file over. NEITHER
      IS CLOSE TO THE CAP, which is the value of knowing rather than assuming: GATES.md ~11,355 tok (~33 KB
      of headroom), PLAN.md ~17,990 tok (~17 KB). PLAN.md is the one to watch — every outstanding entry in
      `decisions` asks for a PLAN.md edit.

  (2) THE ESTIMATOR IS NOW MEASURED FOR MARKDOWN, NOT GUESSED FROM JSON. There is no tokenizer on this
      machine, so the Read tool is the tokenizer: its truncation notice reports the exact total. 179,382
      bytes of real repo markdown = 68,900 tokens = 2.604 B/tok, against iter128's JSON-derived 2.368.
      Markdown is the SPARSER of the two, so iter128's 2.3 over-estimated markdown by ~13% — conservative,
      and its OVER-CAP flags were honest before anyone checked. This mattered because extending the checker
      with a wrong constant would have made it cry wolf on PLAN.md, which is worse than no checker.

  (3) A CORRECTION TO ITER128, because the method rests on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
      "[Truncated: PARTIAL view — showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". The risk is
      an agent skimming past an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything — and that notice is exactly
      what makes offline calibration possible. A bounded Read (limit=2) reports no totals, so the measuring
      Read must be unbounded and you pay for its content.

  (4) THE CHECKER'S RED BRANCHES ARE PROVEN, iter119's lesson applied to a checker that had just tripled its
      FAIL paths. 5/5 fire and name the right file; each case asserts the unmutated copy is GREEN first, so
      a checker that failed on everything could not pass. The harness's own first run scored 3/5 and both
      failures were ITS arithmetic overshooting a 5,000-token band with 45 KB filler, not the checker.

  (5) THE TREE IS GREEN AND THE SANDBOX IS UNCHANGED. `dotnet build` 0 warnings / 0 errors; `dotnet test`
      1361/1361 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (32 s). DOCUMESBX re-probed read-only: 44 pages, histogram
      {1: 43, 2: 1} with `Documentation Status` the only v2, 9 of 12 DocuMe pages carrying an accurate
      `stale` label. Identical to iters 125-128. Seventh clean full run; the iter120 failure did not recur.

  (6) THE PHONE-PUSH CHANNEL IS STILL DEAD AND THE PROTOCOL STILL DOES NOT KNOW IT. iter126 recorded the
      tool answering "Mobile push not sent (Remote Control inactive)", so every gate/blocker push from an
      unattended session most likely went nowhere, while tools/loop/README.md advertises the phone channel
      as live. Keep calling PushNotification (it costs nothing and starts working the moment Remote Control
      is on), but do not count a stalled loop as "reported".

`decisions.mermaidDialectGap`.

**THE CLASS OF WORK THAT IS STILL LEGITIMATE WHEN THE FEATURE BACKLOG IS EMPTY: run the protocol literally
and report what does not work.** iter126 found the dead phone-push channel that way; iter127 found step 1's
Read failing on the byte ceiling; iter128 found it STILL failing on the token cap; iter129 found iter128's

own machinery — the files the protocol reads, the channels it claims, the checks it relies on. It does NOT

end (all three files, per-format constants calibrated against the only tokenizer available, red branches
proven 5/5). `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` is the standing test; run it after editing state.json,

FAILS outright, and handoff-archive.md (80 KB) TRUNCATES. Never Read either whole — `tail -3`, `grep -n

decisions.mermaidDialectGap:
OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER113, BLOCKS NO MILESTONE. beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 (pinned in
package.json) renders `flowchart LR` and `sequenceDiagram` but REJECTS `graph TD;` and `pie`.
The `graph TD;` rejection is caused by the TRAILING SEMICOLON ALONE — `graph TD` renders fine.
Measured one dialect per run at .mtk/paths-113/probe-mermaid-dialects.py; re-runnable in ~30s.
OPTIONS AS WRITTEN INTO GATES.md: (a) upgrade or replace the renderer; (b) strip a trailing `;`
from the header inside tools/render-mermaid.mjs — one line, buys back `graph TD;`, does nothing
for `pie`, and quietly rewrites the user's diagram source; (c) accept both as known-unsupported
dialects and have the converter report them as a NAMED DEGRADATION instead of failing the page.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE GOLDEN CASE: this is PLAN.md §7's deferred question ('how many of the 59
AurServices mermaid diagrams does beautiful-mermaid reject?') arriving at M2 instead of M7, on a
corpus small enough to reason about. Whoever implements the answer should re-run the probe first.

The ends still need a repo with pull requests and, for the refresh half, secrets. OPTIONS: (a) install templates/workflows/docs-drift-pr.yml into .github/workflows/ on THIS repo and open one PR — cheapest, needs no secrets at all, and demonstrates the drift comment; (b) additionally add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + DOCUME_CONFLUENCE_EMAIL/TOKEN as repo secrets and install docs-refresh.yml + docs-publish.yml, which demonstrates the whole chain but makes every push to main publish to the sandbox; (c) fold the acceptance into M7 Aur adoption, where a real repo with real PRs and a real deploy already exists, and reword the §14 criterion to say so. NOTE THIS INTERACTS WITH decisions.pushPolicy: a pull request on this repo presupposes the branch is on GitHub, and origin/main is 93 commits behind.
decisions.pushPolicy: OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER121. Should the loop `git push origin main` as part of an iteration? TODAY IT DOES NOT AND NEVER HAS: origin/main is at 699c855 ("iter74") while local main is at iter120, i.e. [ahead 93]. The protocol says commit, not push, and the loop read that literally. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE UNILATERALLY AT ITER121: 93 commits arriving on Moberg's org fires ci.yml (it triggers on push to main), is visible to anyone watching the repo, and cannot be undone without the history rewrite rule §8.2 forbids. WHAT IT COSTS TO LEAVE: gate-m6's release instructions had to gain a 'push main first' step (a tag push carries its own objects, so the release would build from the tag while the default branch still showed iter74), and M5's PR-based acceptance is not reachable at all until the branch is on GitHub. ANSWER HERE: 'always' (loop pushes every iteration), 'on-request', or 'never' (and then expect to push by hand before each gate that needs the remote).
decisions.planSection6Deviations:
OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER122, BLOCKS NO MILESTONE. PLAN.md §6's preamble says: "Global:
`--config <path>` (default `./docume.json`), `--verbose`, `--json` (machine output)". Measured against
every command's own `--help` at iter122, that sentence is false in three ways, and each needs a direction
rather than a guess:
  (a) `--verbose` IS BUILT NOWHERE. No command takes it and nothing in the repo records a decision to
      drop it. Building it is not mechanical — it means deciding what a verbose run says, across the
      Spectre output and the Confluence client.
  (b) `--json` IS BUILT ON `status` ALONE (StatusCommand.cs). `drift` spells its machine output
      `--format table|json|github-comment` instead, which §6.4 specifies and which covers the same need
      under another name. `init`, `publish`, `sync`, `dashboard` and `convert` have no machine output.
  (c) `--config` IS ABSENT FROM `init` AND `convert`. Both are defensible — `init` writes docume.json in
      the working directory rather than being pointed at one, `convert` takes the wiki root as an argument
      plus `--renderer` — but §6 says global without excepting them.
THE TWO DIRECTIONS: (1) BUILD the missing flags (three slices, (a) the largest); or (2) CORRECT §6's
preamble to say what actually shipped and why (`--json` where a machine consumer exists, `--config` where
there is a config to resolve), which is a spec edit and therefore yours.
WHERE TO PUT THE ANSWER: this field. WHAT I DO THEN: implement it, and STRIKE THE ENTRY OFF
`UnbuiltOptions` in tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanCommandSpecTests.cs — that test fails if a
listed gap is built, so the record cannot drift from reality in either direction.
WHY I DID NOT PICK ONE: rewriting the spec to match the code is how a spec stops being a spec, and §4.3's
rule against regenerating a golden to make a test pass is the same rule one level up. The gap is now
visible and asserted, which is the part that was missing.
decisions.planSection5Deviations:
OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER123, BLOCKS NO MILESTONE. PLAN.md §5.1 declares two config fields that
LOAD, VALIDATE, ROUND-TRIP AND ARE READ BY NO LINE OF src/. A consumer can set either and nothing at all
happens. Each needs a direction rather than a guess:

  (a) `links.repoBlobUrl`. §5.1 declares it ("optional: linkify source refs at baseline SHA"), §6.2 step 2
      SPECIFIES THE BEHAVIOUR ("linkify source refs to `repoBlobUrl@baselineSha` if configured"), and
      plugin/skills/docs-loop/SKILL.md:169 TELLS THE SKILL IT WORKS: "If `docume.json` sets
      `links.repoBlobUrl`, publish linkifies those refs at the baseline sha". A shipped skill asserting a
      behaviour the CLI does not have is why this is worse than iter122's unbuilt flag. OPTIONS: build the
      linkification in the publish path (it is a converter/link-map concern — §6.2 step 2 sits right next
      to the relative-link rewrite that IS built), or strike the promise from §6.2, from the skill and
      from §5.1.
  (b) `drift.defaultBranch`. §5.1 declares it (default "dev") and §10's PR bullet writes `docume drift
      --baseline origin/<defaultBranch>`. No command reads it. templates/workflows/docs-drift-pr.yml
      deliberately computes a MERGE BASE from the pull request instead (its comment even says "that
      setting is for local runs"), and a local `drift` with no --baseline falls back to state.json's
      baselineSha — so the local case does not read it either. OPTIONS: have the no---baseline fallback
      consult it (`origin/<defaultBranch>` before baselineSha, or as the documented default), or drop the
      field from §5.1 and stop §10 implying a branch default exists.

WHERE TO PUT THE ANSWER: this field. WHAT HAPPENS THEN: the loop builds or removes as instructed, and IN
THE SAME SLICE strikes the entry off `DeadFields` in
tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanDataContractTests.cs and deletes its bullet from
docs/wiki/20-reference/configuration.md's "Two fields are inert in this version" section. The test fails
from BOTH sides if only one of those happens, which is deliberate.

WHY THE LOOP DID NOT PICK: rule §4.3 says never regenerate a golden to make a test pass; choosing between
"build the feature" and "delete the promise" is the same rule one level up. iter122 set this precedent for
planSection6Deviations and it holds here.
decisions.planSection9Deviation: OPEN, ITER124, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — may PLAN.md §9's CI-posture bullet and rule §1.5 be reworded? THE FACT: both say feedback processing runs with "read-only repo access + PR-only writes". No GitHub job can have read-only repo access AND open a PR from a branch — pushing docs/feedback-<date> needs `contents: write`, and templates/workflows/docs-feedback.yml grants exactly that (contents: write + pull-requests: write) with a comment at the permissions block saying why. Nothing is mis-built: the job never pushes to the default branch and holds no Confluence credentials at all, and docs/wiki/30-automation/workflows.md ALREADY words it correctly ("none of them pushes to the default branch"). So the plan and the rule are the wrong two, and no consumer-facing page needs touching. WHAT I NEED: a yes/no here, or a rewording. WHERE: this field. Step 1 of the protocol opens tools/loop/state.json, GATES.md and PLAN.md §14. iter128 built tools/loop/check-state-size.py for the file it had just fixed and stopped there, so two of the three were guarded by nothing — the same unmeasured-assumption shape that let the token cap truncate step 1 unnoticed between iter127 and iter128, one file over. PLAN.md is the one to watch — every outstanding entry in `decisions` asks for a PLAN.md edit. CALIBRATED THE ESTIMATOR FIRST, because extending a checker with a wrong constant makes it cry wolf on the spec file, which is worse than no checker. No tokenizer exists on this machine (tiktoken, anthropic, transformers all absent), so THE READ TOOL IS THE TOKENIZER: its truncation notice reports the file's exact total. 179,382 bytes of real repo markdown = 68,900 tokens = 2.604 B/tok, against iter128's JSON-derived 2.368 — markdown is the SPARSER of the two, so iter128's 2.3 over-estimated markdown by ~13%, conservative, and its OVER-CAP flags were honest before anyone checked. Rebuild the measurement with .mtk/paths-129/calibrate-read-tokens.py (reproduces the file byte-for-byte). A CORRECTION TO ITER128, because the method rests on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT — the tool prints '[Truncated: PARTIAL view — showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]'. The risk is an agent skimming past an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything, and that notice is exactly what makes offline calibration possible. A bounded Read (limit=2) reports no totals, so the measuring Read must be unbounded and you pay for its content. CHECKER CHANGES: guards all three step-1 files with a per-format constant (JSON 2.3, markdown 2.5, both rounded down from measurement so it trips early not late); prints HEADROOM IN KB per file, the actionable number rather than a pass/fail; separates the two ceilings, which reclassified done-archive.jsonl from 'OVER CAP - TRUNCATES' to 'OVER BYTE CEILING - Read FAILS' (406 KB — it fails outright and that needs different handling); reports CLAUDE.md + ITERATION-PROMPT.md as always-loaded context that spends the window without truncating step 1.
